reason: Re-opened packet.js tanakh 45 --verse 8:2. Rashi's half stands (first comment on בהעלתך: חלשה דעתו ... שלך גדולה משלהם שאתה מדליק ומטיב את הנרות). The Ramban half misattributes: the Hanukkah allusion is not Ramban's reading of the charge but his explanation of the aggadah Rashi quotes ('אבל ענין ההגדה הזו, לדרוש רמז מן הפרשה על חנוכה'), which he says he found in Rabbeinu Nissim's Megillat Setarim citing a midrash, and in Yelamdenu and Numbers Rabbah ('לא רמזו אלא לנרות חנכת חשמונאי': THEY, the sages, alluded). Ramban's own reading of the passage is different: its place completes the laws of the lamps, all seven burning in the candelabrum for all generations ('אבל הסדור בפרשיות האלה הוא ... השלים עוד כל דיני הנרות'). As written ('and Ramban, on 8:2, as alluding to the Hanukkah lights') the sentence makes the midrashic allusion Ramban's own reading of the verse. verse.js ok (Numbers 8:2, at [124,2]) and entry-check ok; plain sense faithful (7:84 to 7:88 princes' dedication, 8:1 the LORD to Moses).
better: After the princes’ dedication gifts, the LORD gives Moses a charge for Aaron; Rashi, on 8:2, reads it as God consoling Aaron, grieved at having no part in that dedication, with the greater task of the lamps, and Ramban, on 8:2, takes that midrash as alluding to the Hanukkah lights of Aaron’s Hasmonean descendants, kept even after the Temple’s destruction. (60 words; the 59-word form without 'greater' passes entry-check.)
